summary: Iteration 12 verified the refactor + account PIN work. Backend: 7/8 pytest cases pass (test_account_and_refresh.py). All account/name + 4-digit PIN flows (A/B/C) + validation + /api/live/analyze shared helper + watched /analyze + refresh-missing-url=400 pass. ONE CRITICAL BUG: POST /api/auctions/{id}/refresh crashes with HTTP 500 because server.py line 613 calls `crawler.compute_fees(...)` but `crawler` is a `Crawler` instance (server.py line 32: `crawler = Crawler(db)`) and `compute_fees` is a MODULE-level function in crawler.py (line 57), not a method on the class. AttributeError confirmed in backend logs. Frontend: app rename to 'Auktiomera.se' is live in both <title> and <h1>; all three tabs (view-live/view-search/view-watch) switch without JS errors; live feed shows auction cards; empty-state restore panel on 'Mina bevakningar' renders data-testid='restore-name-input', 'restore-pin-input' and 'restore-name-button', typing a non-existent name + clicking Hämta triggered the API and the Swedish 'Hittade inget konto med det namnet' toast appeared.

critical.issue: AttributeError: 'Crawler' object has no attribute 'compute_fees' -> HTTP 500. The call `crawler.compute_fees(doc['source'], new_bid, doc)` at server.py:613 should be `compute_fees(...)` (module-level, already used elsewhere, e.g. crawler.py:273, 340, 412) OR imported as `from crawler import compute_fees`. Trivial one-line fix.

rca of the issue: During the refactor the author wrote `crawler.compute_fees(doc['source'], new_bid, doc)` assuming `crawler` refers to the module. But in server.py line 32 the name `crawler` is bound to a `Crawler(db)` INSTANCE (via `from crawler import Crawler`). `compute_fees` lives at the module level (crawler.py:57) and is not a method on the class, so the attribute lookup fails at request time, producing an unhandled AttributeError -> HTTP 500. Reproduction: register push token, POST /api/live/watch any live url, then POST /api/auctions/{id}/refresh — observe 500 and the traceback in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log. Fix: either `from crawler import Crawler, compute_fees` and call `compute_fees(...)`, or `import crawler as crawler_mod` and use `crawler_mod.compute_fees(...)`.
